question: Do the Action Plan and the MPRs address all potential pollution contributors on the Shimsha stretch?
intro: The Shimsha's CPCB polluted stretch runs Yediyur to Halagur bridge (Priority IV). This matrix compares the KSPCB Action Plan's commitments with what the monthly progress reports actually report. 'Not reported' means absent from the documents, not necessarily absent on the ground.

primary.label: NMCG Monthly Progress Report (Karnataka, Shimsha stretch)
primary.note: June 2025 is the last stretch-wise MPR edition we hold for this stretch.

actionPlan.label: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Shimsha (mirrored)

baseline.banner: MPR editions from October 2025 onward no longer report stretch-wise status - accountability tracking anchors on the last stretch-wise reporting.
otherSources: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report (October 2025, mirrored)

solid-waste.label: NGT OA 606/2018 - SWM Rules compliance (Justice Subhash B Adi committee)

biomedical.label: NGT OA 710/2017 - BMW Rules 2016 (KSPCB guidelines hub)

fecal-sludge.label: SC (2017) 5 SCC 326 - mandatory sewage treatment infrastructure; NGT OA 673/2018 monitoring

public-stps.label: SC (2017) 5 SCC 326 - mandatory treatment infrastructure; NGT OA 673/2018 monthly reporting

effluent.label: Water Act consent regime; KSPCB hazardous waste management

regions.name: Maddur (TMC)
regions.inBasinNote: The stretch ULB - population 28,902, on the Bengaluru-Mysuru corridor.

categories.label: Public STPs

actionPlan.summary: 100% UGD for the town, a terminal STP to CPCB standards, no untreated discharge, treated sewage to irrigation (actions 1-3); a 3.5 MLD low-cost facility already existed in 2019.

mpr.summary: The stretch's good-news story: 3.5 MLD generated, 3.5 MLD STP fully utilised, operational and COMPLIED, gap nil. The Rs 50.15 crore upgrade to 6 MLD is reported completed and under operation; household connections (4,000 houses) and wet wells still in progress.

gaps: Storm-water-drain diversion and the extension-area network remain 'in progress' - the plan's 'no sewage into storm drains' commitment is not yet closed.
Compliance is a single word per edition; no parameter-level trail.

categories.label: Solid Waste

actionPlan.summary: MSW including poultry and slaughter-house waste to be disposed only at MSW sites, never on the river banks (action 4); the plan records ~9 TPD generation and bank dumping.

mpr.summary: 10 TPD generated; 70% of wet waste home-composted, 30% at a decentralised plant; dry waste sold to scrap dealers; a 7-acre landfill site provided at Huthgere under 15th Finance grants - but composting shows a 4.1 TPD gap, landfill a 2.4 TPD gap, and the site's authorisation is reported expired.

gaps: The landfill authorisation lapse is reported but carries no renewal status.
Slaughter-house and poultry waste - specifically named in the plan - has no dedicated reporting line.

actionPlan.summary: Biomedical waste does not appear in the Shimsha Action Plan.
actionPlan.cite: Shimsha Action Plan (full text, zero mentions)

mpr.summary: 81.7 kg/day across 3 bedded and 26 non-bedded facilities; disposed to CBMWTF (M/s Maridi Eco Solutions).

categories.label: Fecal Sludge

actionPlan.summary: Faecal sludge and septage do not appear in the Action Plan.

mpr.summary: Households not yet on the UGD (4,000 connections still in progress) have no reported septage route.

gaps: Until the network closes, the unconnected households' septage is the unaccounted flow.

mpr.summary: No private STP reporting for Maddur in any edition.

regions.name: Industry on the stretch
regions.inBasinNote: The plan tables industrial units within 5 km of the river; the MPR reports one water-polluting industry on the stretch.

categories.label: Industrial effluent

actionPlan.summary: Category-wise inventory of units within 5 km of the river, with treatment status per unit.

mpr.summary: One water-polluting industry reported, generating 2.9 MLD of effluent with its own ETP - a single source producing nearly as much effluent as the entire town's sewage (3.5 MLD).

gaps: One factory ~ one town in effluent terms, yet its compliance is a single line with no published effluent data or continuous monitoring.

regions.name: Gram Panchayats (Shimsha stretch)
regions.inBasinNote: The rural tank-cascade country between Yediyur and Halagur.
regions.silentNote: No MPR edition and no Action Plan item reports anything at gram-panchayat level for this stretch - in the basin's largest tank country (222 MI tanks), the rural reach is unreported in the official accountability trail.
